title: A hundred camels
hookLine: the sirah tells how Abd al-Muttalib's vow to sacrifice a son was ransomed with a hundred camels, and the son was Abdullah

lines: A VOW IN A HARD MOMENT.
TEN SONS, AND ONE TO GIVE.
cards: A vow, made in a hard moment.

The sirah says that while Abd al-Muttalib was digging Zamzam, with one son beside him and the men of Quraysh against him, he promised God: if I am given ten sons who grow up to stand by me, I will sacrifice one of them at the House.
Years pass. The sons come. They grow up.
And a father now has to face a promise that has names and faces. Today: a hundred camels.

teach.b: He gathered his sons, the sirah says, told them of the vow, and they agreed. Lots were cast at the House with marked arrows, and the lot fell on Abdullah, the youngest, his father's favorite.
He led the boy toward the place of sacrifice.
And Mecca stopped him. Quraysh, and the boy's family on his mother's side, stood in his way: if you do this, they said, men will start bringing their sons here to sacrifice. Find another way.
They sent him to a woman people consulted on hard questions. She asked what the blood-money was among them. Ten camels.
Then cast lots, she said, between the boy and ten camels. If the lot falls on the boy, add ten more, and keep going until your Lord is satisfied. They cast.

On and on, until at a hundred camels the lot fell on the camels. The sirah says he cast it three more times to be sure, and each time it fell on the camels. They were slaughtered and left for anyone to eat.
Abdullah lived, and he would become the father of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ. Some who tell this story hear in it an echo of Ibrahim, who was told to sacrifice his son and was stopped.
In surah thirty-seven, Pickthall translates that moment: "Then We ransomed him with a tremendous victim."

teach.h: WE RANSOMED HIM WITH A TREMENDOUS VICTIM.
teach.b: Ransomed: a life paid for with something else. The sirah leaves a picture close to it: a son walking away from the altar alive, and later, a ransomed father.

how: The story of Abdullah's ransom is told in the sirah books and in mosque classes on the Prophet's family, and the sacrifice at Eid al-Adha remembers Ibrahim's ransomed son.

games.q: you're Abd al-Muttalib. the lot has fallen on your son Abdullah, and Quraysh block your way. what does the woman they sent you to tell you to do?

cast lots between the boy and camels, adding ten each time.
go home and forget the vow.
games.why: the sirah says the lot kept falling on Abdullah until a hundred camels, and then it turned.

practice: Bring to mind a life that was spared, maybe your own in a near miss or an illness that turned, maybe someone you love who came through when they might not have, and let the memory come without the fear, just the fact of it: they are here, you are here.
If you pray, you can thank Allah for that life in your own words; if you don't, simply let gratitude sit where the fear once was.

wordCard.voice: Abdullah. Abd al-Muttalib's youngest and favorite son, the one the lot kept choosing, ransomed at last by a hundred camels. Today's word.
